checks.claim: Subtitle configuration has its own setting branch, while subtitle startup reuses global API and prompt resources.
If exact language/kind matching fails, this selector can choose a different track instead of preserving a strict selected-track identity.
The boundary mapping can merge multiple input events into one output cue, so it is not necessarily one input cue to one translated cue.
Editable prompt contents can select the subtitle wire protocol in this reference implementation.
In the nonlegacy boundary parser, one invalid boundary stops parsing later entries rather than retaining all later individually valid entries.

The shown seek handlers cancel translation throttling but do not invalidate translation session identity or explicitly abort in-flight requests; the callback only directly rerenders if its subtitle object is currently active.

In the shown ordinary-translation cache key construction, service URL and model are not directly included; its prompt digest also does not include these fields. This claim does not cover other cache paths.

The batch queue key shown does not isolate video/session identity, and batch execution forwards the first task args to its function; therefore per-task cancellation ownership is not independently forwarded by this batching layer.
When translation is absent, the shown translation-only display path renders an ellipsis rather than original text.
